title: Ephemeral Proxying & Region Fallback Playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This document describes an operational playbook for ephemeral proxying as a short-lived mitigation when region pin enforcement fails or when residency routing is temporarily unavailable. The goal is to keep customer writes (or sensitive reads) compliant while minimizing downtime and producing auditable evidence for legal/regulatory needs.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployments and Dedicated customers with strict region pins.
- Assumes runtime supports a proxy layer capable of routing traffic based on tenant metadata and that we can toggle proxying via feature flag.
- This is a mitigation, not a long-term substitute for fixing region pin enforcement bugs.
- Operator privileges required: residency-ops, infra-oncall, and legal-notify.

When to use ephemeral proxying:
- Region pin routing service (region-gateway) returns 5xx or times out across multiple zones for a tenant with hard pin.
- Evidence of cross-border routing detected in telemetry (see "signals" below).
- Customer requests temporary failover during a verified cloud provider outage.

High-level flow:
1) Detection: automated alert or manual customer report triggers assessment.
2) Triage: confirm scope, impact, and whether proxying is acceptable per contract.
3) Enable ephemeral proxy: create per-tenant proxy rule that forces traffic to a pre-authorized anchoring site.
4) Audit capture: record request headers, route decision logs, and signed evidence package for the legal team.
5) Monitor: increased telemetry sampling and SLO checks.
6) Rollback: revert proxy rules once region routing restored and evidence validated.

Detection signals (telemetry):
- Sudden spike in region-mismatch errors: count(region_assertion != tenant_pin) > 0.5% over 5m for a high-volume tenant.
- route_decision_timeouts >= 3 consecutive failures for tenant_id in 1m window.
- Sampled request traces showing egress IPs outside pinned subnets.
Suggested telemetry queries (pseudo-SQL):
- SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as mismatches FROM routing_logs WHERE region_assertion != tenant_pin AND ts > now()-5m GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY mismatches DESC LIMIT 20;
- SELECT tenant_id, avg(route_decision_latency_ms) FROM routing_metrics WHERE ts > now()-1m GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING avg(route_decision_latency_ms) > 500;

Pre-checks before enabling proxying:
- Verify customer's contract allows temporary routing exceptions. If not, escalate to legal.
- Check pre-authorized anchoring locations for the tenant (from tenant_metadata).
- Ensure KMS/HSM key locality constraints are satisfied for writes; if not, proxying is a no-go.
- Confirm audit logging pipeline is healthy (elk/audit-bucket writable).

How to enable ephemeral proxy (operator steps):
1) Create proxy rule (example CLI):
   redwoodctl proxy create --tenant TENANT_ID --type ephemeral --target-region eu-anchoring-1 --ttl 01:00:00 --reason "region-gateway failures 2024-03-04"
   Note: default TTL is 1 hour. Use conservative durations.
2) Enable elevated telemetry sampling for tenant:
   redwoodctl telemetry set-sampling --tenant TENANT_ID --rate 1.0 --notes "ephemeral-proxying"
3) Capture evidence bundle: route-decision logs, ingress headers, egress IP list, and signed operator approval. Save to: s3://residency-evidence/TENANT_ID/YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.zip
4) Post a short entry to #residency-ops with tenant, action taken, link to evidence.

Operator approval template (copy into log):
- Operator: NAME
- Time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ
- Trigger: automated-alert / customer-report
- Impacted tenant: TENANT_ID
- Reason for proxy: short summary
- Target anchor: REGION_ID
- Expected TTL: 1h
- Legal notified: yes/no (include timestamp)

Customer-visible behavior while proxied:
- Writes are routed to anchor region; reads may be served from cache depending on config.
- API response header: X-Redwood-Residency-Proxy: true
- Short-lived session cookie change may cause higher tail latency for first few requests.

Audit and evidence collection:
- Always include signed route-decision snapshot with operator signature.
- Evidence package should include: routing_logs (last 24h), route_decision_snapshots, operator_approval.txt, telemetry-sample.json (1% full traces), and health-check outputs for region-gateway.
- Evidence filename convention: TENANTID_PROXY_EVIDENCE_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.zip

Edge cases & constraints:
- If tenant has enclave-only KMS keys (HSM in-region), proxying must not be used unless legal/crypto approves rewrapping keys.
- For multi-tenant physical hosts, ensure proxy rules scope only the tenant to avoid cross-tenant data movement.
- If the anchoring region is under a different compliance regime, run the legal checklist before action.

Rollback and verification:
- Use redwoodctl proxy status --tenant TENANT_ID to confirm route decisions are healthy.
- Gradual rollback recommended: change TTL to 10m then to 0.
- Verify no route_mismatch events for 15 minutes post-rollback. Run: SELECT count(*) FROM routing_logs WHERE region_assertion != tenant_pin AND ts > now()-15m AND tenant_id = 'TENANT_ID'; Expect 0.

Post-incident tasks (OWNER: infra-oncall):
- Create postmortem ticket linking incident alerts, evidence package, and root cause hypothesis.
- If proxying used, ask legal to review evidence package and flag any contract concerns.
- Create remediation PRs if the failure was due to missing region-metadata, timeouts, or caching issues (link: PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/ephemeral-proxy-remediation-template).

Operator checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm contract allowance or legal OK
- [ ] Verify anchor region KMS compatibility
- [ ] Create proxy rule with minimal TTL
- [ ] Increase telemetry sampling and capture evidence
- [ ] Notify #residency-ops and customer success
- [ ] Monitor for 15m, then plan rollback

Example curl snippet to detect proxy header (for QA):
curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep X-Redwood-Residency-Proxy

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Operator error enables long-lived proxying. Mitigation: enforce TTL <= 4h for manual creates and auto-expire rules older than 6h.
- Risk: Evidence pipeline failure (cannot produce audit bundle). Mitigation: block proxy creation if audit-bucket returns non-200 on pre-check.
- Risk: Unintended data residency policy drift. Mitigation: require legal signoff for >2h proxy periods and automated daily compliance report showing all proxy events.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add per-tenant allowlist for emergency anchors in tenant metadata UI (ticket JIRA-8123).
- Automate legal notification via PagerDuty integration when proxying is enabled for >30m.
- Add canned Kibana dashboard for ephemeral-proxy events (owner: Lina).

Appendix: quick links
- Region pin design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Region+Pinning+Design
- Residency alert runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Residency+Alerts
- Jira escalation: JIRA-7892

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally operational and lightweight — meant to be used by oncall and SRE during short outages. Please add missing legal checks or contract language examples if you know them.
summary: Operational playbook for temporary per-tenant proxying to maintain data residency during routing failures. Includes detection signals, operator commands, audit evidence checklist, rollback steps, and open action items.
